items.title: Turn on your live pin
items.detail: Install OwnTracks and open your private setup link. In iPhone Settings, set OwnTracks Location to Always and turn Precise Location on. Publish once and check the Where tab.

items.title: Confirm PCA entry and doubles with Alex
items.detail: The PCA entry list (as of Nov 18) shows “Sy, Jerry” (#159), no “Shi”. Entries close Sat Nov 21. If Alex can’t confirm fast, call PCA 8563 8501 ext 116 or email philcolumbian_pcaopen@yahoo.com.
items.draft: Hey Alex, PCA posted the entry list and I see “Sy, Jerry” (#159) but no “Shi”. Is that me? Entries close Saturday. Also is doubles with Tom in, and when does doubles start?

items.title: Decide Tokyo dates
items.detail: Contacts have heard ~Dec 1 (Shingo), ~Dec 3 (Jinji, Tom); the app says ~Dec 5 or Dec 14. Depends on PCA (main draw Dec 5–13) and landing LAX by Dec 6–7. Diadora Cup (Dec 15) only fits the late option. TTI, Jinji, Ryoto, Shingo and new Tokyo contacts wait on this.

items.detail: He offered a hit at Valle Verde (IG, Nov 18).
items.draft: Valle Verde sounds good! I land Saturday night, I’ll message you when I get in.

items.title: Migi · when are qualies
items.detail: She asked when PCA qualies are (IG, Nov 18).
items.draft: Qualies are Nov 30 to Dec 4! No worries at all, any tune-up games you find would be awesome. Thank you!

items.title: Marvin · confirm 43rd PCA
items.detail: He replied “43rd pca open” and offered to arrange courts (IG).
items.draft: Yes it’s the 43rd PCA Open, qualies Nov 30. I’m in Manila from Nov 21. Would love that court hit before qualies.

items.detail: He sent the 2026 PHILTA Men’s National Open post and asked “R u talking about this tournament?” (IG, Nov 19).
items.draft: It’s this tournament: https://www.abs-cbn.com/sports/othersports/2026/10/15/local-tennis-players-take-the-spotlight-at-43rd-pca-open-1348 But I’m down to hit in Cebu after!

items.draft: Sorry, I meant Manila! I’m there from Nov 21. Could we set a hit with one of your coaches that week?

items.title: Tokyo Tennis International · price check, no booking
items.detail: ¥16,000/h ≈ $100/h (Nov 19 rate) at Hilton Tokyo; 100% fee under 24h; card deposit. Only verified high level: Lilian Breut (ATP career high 1321, 2022). Jelassi Mourad claims Tunisia Davis Cup (unverified). Others are coaches. Optional reply asks for Lilian or Jelassi without booking.

Filip様、Kazu様

ご返信ありがとうございます。日程はまだ調整中です。プライベートの場合、Lilianさんか Jelassiさんとの試合形式の練習は可能でしょうか。

items.title: Finish eTravel and save the QR
items.detail: For the scheduled PR123 arrival, the 72-hour window opened Wednesday, Nov 18 at 10:45 PM Manila time (6:45 AM Pacific). Use the official free form and save the QR.

items.title: Confirm the listing and onward plan
items.detail: PR123 replaces PR103 in the current plan. Check the actual listing or ticket, passport validity and what proof of onward travel PAL will accept.

items.title: Confirm and book the return flight
items.detail: Aim to land at LAX by Sun Dec 6. Mon Dec 7 works only if the later deadline is confirmed. Check Tokyo and Manila departures, and keep a confirmed backup if using the AA companion standby listing. Reconcile Japan and PCA dates before booking.

items.title: Pack light and hand off Alex’s gear
items.detail: Confirm Alex’s racket and strings for Adelmo, and check how the racket box must be packed. Bring your playing gear, everyday pants and hoodie, and Shingo’s sticker. Leave the orange puffer.

items.title: Set up phone service and offline trip info
items.detail: Install the eSIM on Wi-Fi if needed. Save the pickup details, reservations and contact routes offline. Clear work-laptop travel with IT if bringing it.

items.detail: Confirm a session or book a public court if the club sessions don’t line up.

plan.sub: With Jerry, dates depend on PCA

bucket: Bring the bomber jacket and get patchwork or a cool graphic print done

items.title: Install the Trip iPhone app (TestFlight)
items.detail: Install TestFlight. Open the private invite Jerry shares after Apple approves the beta. Tap Install and turn on Automatic Updates in TestFlight. Plan edits refresh in Trip.

items.title: Turn on your live pin
items.detail: Install OwnTracks and open your private setup link. In iPhone Settings, set OwnTracks Location to Always and turn Precise Location on. Publish once and check the Where tab.

items.title: Sync Cebu, Siargao and Manila with Jerry
items.detail: Keep Cebu arrival as planned. Set Siargao and Manila around actual doubles eligibility and dates. Tell Jerry when you can overlap.

items.title: Pick one bandana or neck-scarf sample
items.detail: Bring one sample and a clear photo. Show what the print, fabric or edge does in use. Use Little Tokyo Table Tennis as a starting point for color and ask one question about how a maker gets a piece from drawing to sample.

items.title: Start with Shingo at Setinn
items.detail: @sng1980 · Setinn director and BEAMS buyer. Reconnect from the LA event, show one sample and ask for one maker he would recommend. Mention Shingo to others once the meeting or introduction is confirmed.
items.draft: Hey Shingo, it’s Tom. We met at the BEAMS event in LA with Jerry. Could I stop by Setinn when I’m in Tokyo and show you a tennis bandana I’m working on? I’d also love your read on one local maker who’s good at taking a graphic from a sketch to a wearable sample.

items.title: Kazue Mizushima · Ask for one introduction
items.detail: LA stylist and WWD Japan contributor. She works across LA and Tokyo. Use her site’s contact page to ask who develops patterns and first samples for a small Tokyo label.
items.draft: Hi Kazue, I’m Tom Oh in LA. I’m working on a tennis bandana and trying to understand how small Tokyo labels go from a sketch to a first sample. Is there one pattern maker or sample maker you’d point me to? I can send a photo so you can see what I’m working on. Thanks.

items.title: Ask Pilgrim Tokyo about their bandanas
items.detail: A real surf-to-everyday clothing connection. Start with the Tokyo shop and its Spring/Summer bandana. Ask who works on accessories.
items.draft: Hi, I’m Tom, a designer from LA. I saw the bandana in your spring/summer collection and liked how it fits in with the rest of the surf pieces. I’m making a bandana for tennis. Is there someone on the Tokyo team I could show a sample to when I stop by?

items.title: Ask Sillage about fabric and finishing
items.detail: Use the Daikanyama shop or business email. Start with the Artisanal patchwork process. Bring the sample if they’re interested.
items.draft: Hi Sillage team, I’m Tom, a designer from LA. I liked how you turn old workwear into patchwork for the Circular Pants. I’m working on tennis bandanas and thinking about how the fabric and edges will wear. Would it be okay to stop by the shop and show you one?

items.title: Ask Mountain Martial Arts about running gear
items.detail: Use the brand’s contact form. Ask how they test fabric and print in motion. Offer a photo and ask about visiting only if it’s convenient.
items.draft: Hi MMA team, I’m Tom, a designer from LA. I came across your Racing Series. I’m working on a bandana for tennis and I’m curious how your team tests what actually works during a run. Can I send you a photo of the sample? If you’re around while I’m in Tokyo, coffee’s on me.

items.title: Jun Takahashi · UNDERCOVER Aoyama
items.detail: Follow @joniotakahashi and study SS03 SCAB, his Paris debut. The hand-stitched patches change how the clothes drape. His GRACE characters and the 2015 Supreme × UNDERCOVER sticker show his work off the garment. Visit or call Aoyama at +81 3 5778 4805 to ask about an archive or book.
items.draft: Hi, I’m Tom from LA. I’m studying how the layered stitching in UNDERCOVER’s SS03 SCAB changes the shape of the clothes. Is there a book, archive, or anything in the Aoyama shop you’d recommend I look at while I’m in Tokyo? Thanks.

items.title: Yu Kimura · KIMRA
items.detail: Spent over a decade at UNDERCOVER, including menswear and accessories production. KIMRA’s debut drew on 1990s European hardcore techno and included a cap with a neck shade and removable sweatband. Ask through KIMRA’s form about how that accessory reached its first sample.
items.draft: Hi Kimura-san, I’m Tom Oh from LA. I saw the KIMRA cap with the neck shade and removable sweatband. I’m making a tennis bandana and working out how it should feel after an hour on court. Would you have time for a short coffee in Tokyo to talk about what you test on a first sample?

items.title: Takayuki Fujii · nonnative
items.detail: @takayuki_fujii_ · Co-created OZISM with Takahashi, taking cues from Yasujirō Ozu and samue workwear. Start with the easy fit and wrap construction. Good reference for making an experimental idea feel like everyday clothes.
items.draft: Hi Fujii-san, I’m Tom from LA. I like how the wrap and relaxed fit in OZISM feel like clothes you’d actually reach for every day. Is there one piece from the project you’d tell me to try on in Tokyo to understand the cut?

items.title: Tetsuya Nagato · UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION
items.detail: @tetsuyanagato · Co-directed UNDERCOVER’s 35th-anniversary behind-the-scenes film. Follow how he turns studio work and fittings into a story. Start with the Tokyo chapter of but beautiful 4… and ask how he chooses what to show from the making process.
items.draft: Hi Nagato-san, I’m Tom from LA. In the Tokyo chapter of but beautiful 4…, I liked seeing the work at the atelier before the looks went to Paris. I’m documenting my own first samples. How do you decide which parts of the process are worth showing?

items.title: VERDY · Graphic artist
items.detail: @verdy · Follow the Last Orgy 2 varsity jacket with UNDERCOVER and HUMAN MADE. Good reference for moving a recognizable graphic into a garment without losing the original drawing’s character.

items.title: NIGO · NOWHERE and HUMAN MADE
items.detail: @nigo · Opened NOWHERE with Takahashi and founded BAPE. Study how their Last Orgy 2 magazine work became apparel. If Shingo can introduce you, ask for one person from that scene who still works hands-on with samples.

items.title: Tetsu Nishiyama · WTAPS
items.detail: @Tetsu_Nishiyama · Follow his 2025 WTAPS × UNDERCOVER project. They made seven shirts from a shared interest in Kurosawa’s Seven Samurai. Compare how Nishiyama treats the characters as graphics and Takahashi takes them into jacquard.

items.title: Shunta Nakajima · ALMOSTBLACK
items.detail: info@sndo.jp · Worked as an assistant designer for Raf Simons in Antwerp, then co-founded ALMOSTBLACK. Start with his Kazuo Shiraga project to see how he puts Japanese art into wearable clothes. Best direct Raf connection for Tom’s mix of graphics and tailoring.
items.draft: Hi Nakajima-san, I’m Tom Oh from LA. I saw your Kazuo Shiraga project and liked how the gesture in the painting still comes through on the clothes. I’m working through the same problem on a much smaller scale with a tennis bandana. Would you have time for a quick coffee in Tokyo to talk about how you decide what to carry over from the artwork?

items.title: Yuki Hashimoto · Design assistant to Raf
items.detail: info@yuki-hashimoto.com · Assisted Raf Simons, Kris Van Assche and Maison Margiela while studying in Antwerp. Look at his Washed Twisted Work Pants to see where a changed seam alters a familiar shape.
items.draft: Hi Hashimoto-san, I’m Tom from LA. I like that your Twisted Work Pants still read as workwear, even though the leg looks different when you move. When you try a cut like that, what do you look for in the first fitting? I’d love to hear your take if you have time for a coffee in Tokyo.

items.title: Taro Horiuchi · th products Sendagaya
items.detail: th_sendagaya@a-tconcepts.com · Raf Simons backstage assistant from 2004 to 2007. He now runs th products. Visit the Sendagaya shop near Setinn and ask which piece best shows his approach to cutting.
items.draft: Hi th products team, I’m Tom from LA. I’ll be near Sendagaya on my Tokyo trip and would like to stop by. Is there one piece you’d recommend trying on to understand how Horiuchi-san approaches fit and proportion? Thanks.

items.title: Koichi Tamaki · Pattern maker
items.detail: @pattern_maker_tamaki · Ready-to-wear pattern maker who shares construction and toile work. Ask whether a workshop fits your dates and whether you can bring a sample. The workshop schedule needs confirmation.
items.draft: Hi Tamaki-san, I’m Tom from LA. I’ve been looking at your posts about how a garment is put together. Do you have a pattern workshop coming up that a beginner could join? I can bring a small sample if useful.

items.title: Soshi Otsuki · SOSHIOTSUKI
items.detail: @soshiotsuki · Uses Japanese classical performing arts as a starting point for menswear tailoring. Compare the shoulder and drape of his suits with what you like in Armani and Yohji. Follow his label or approach through its public contact route.

items.title: Hideki Ozono · Spotted Horse Craft
items.detail: Osaka denim maker. His studio sews in-house and finishes denim by hand. Follow how a single pair goes through sewing and ageing. Use the studio’s Contact link to ask about one finish or a public workshop.
items.draft: Hi Ozono-san, I’m Tom Oh from LA. I’m interested in how you get a worn finish by hand. Is there a particular pair or video you’d recommend to see how the denim changes from the first wash to the final finish? Thanks.

items.title: BAPE COLLECTIVE · Ask who made the sample
items.detail: Official BAPE Japan contact form. Ask who handled the samples for BAPE by KidSuper, starting with the flipped shark hoodie. The show is a reference Tom named himself. Ask for the production team or a public event.
items.draft: Hi BAPE team, I’m Tom Oh from LA. I’ve been studying the flipped shark hoodie from BAPE by KidSuper and am curious who turned that design into the runway sample. Is there a public talk, interview, or production credit I could look up? Thanks.

items.title: TENEZ booth at Tokyo Big Sight · Dec 8–9
items.detail: 2026 Good Work Creation Fair, South Hall 3–4, booth A-186. Dec 8 10:00–17:00, Dec 9 10:00–16:00. The Tomita twins (tennis players) will be there; team runs from 10 pieces. Bring the bandana sample.
items.draft: Hey! I’m Tom, a designer from LA who plays a lot of tennis. I’m making a tennis bandana and I’ll be in Tokyo in December. Planning to swing by your booth at Big Sight on the 8th or 9th. Could I show you a sample and ask how you handle small team runs? Down to hit too.

items.title: Koichi Tamaki pattern workshop · Dec 10–13
items.detail: Tomigaya, Shibuya, ¥5,000, about 2 hours, in Japanese. Open to people outside the trade. Apply through tamasan.com and bring the sample.

items.title: BOLOCO at Kamawanu Asakusa · Dec 4–20
items.detail: Sakiori pop-up 10:00–18:00, closed Tue. Weaving workshop Dec 5–6, 2 seats per session, ¥8,800: bring a towel or bandana to weave into a 35×50 cm piece. Book by phone 03-6231-6466.

items.title: Yuta Sugimoto · Small Lighter
items.detail: Bandana-only label founder in Shibuya. Hand-screened reactive dye.
items.draft: Hi Yuta, I’m Tom from LA. I make bandanas for tennis and running, and Small Lighter’s factory page is the best thing I’ve read on how bandanas are made. I’ll be in Tokyo in December. Could I buy you a coffee and trade you one of mine?

items.title: Mizuno Dyeing · OKUROJI meeting
items.detail: Custom tenugui from 5 pieces; lead time 2–3 weeks, so it may not be ready before you leave.
items.draft: Individual designer from LA, in Tokyo in December. I’d like to discuss a small run (10–30) of a bandana-size cloth from my artwork. Could I book a meeting at OKUROJI?

items.title: CHAORAS · edge and fabric
items.detail: Sports tenugui (Osaka). Email before arriving.
items.draft: Hi, I’m Tom, a designer in LA making a tennis bandana. I read your YAMAP interview about the overlocked edge and the cotton/bamboo-rayon fabric. That’s exactly what I’m stuck on. Do you take small original orders from overseas designers?

items.title: Shibui · Guerrilla Run
items.detail: Watch @mountainmartialarts Stories for a run date.
items.draft: Hi Shibui-san, I’m Tom from LA. I run and I’m making a bandana for tennis and running. If there’s a Tokyo Guerrilla Run while I’m there in December, I’d love to join. Can I send you a photo of my sample?

items.title: Tokyo Wasarashi · dyeing class
items.detail: Katsushika chusen dye works; open 9:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00.
items.draft: Hello, I’m Tom, a designer from LA. I’d like to book a tenugui dyeing class in December and ask whether you do small chusen runs (around 100) of an original design.
